entities.name: Judy Health
entities.how_described: 本集说它是一个健康福利管理方,从药品福利(PBM)切入,收固定费用、所有人拿到同样的药价,后来愿景是做「医疗保健的 ERP」;早期名字叫 Capital RX,去年完成 4 亿美元融资、估值超 30 亿美元。

evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: You know, so if a traditional pharmacy benefit manager, someone we compete with, they'll have hundreds of different prices for the same drug, same day, same pharmacy for different customers.

entities.name: 垂直整合 (vertically integrated)
entities.how_described: 本集说行业巨头不只做管理方,还拥有药房、返点聚合业务,从而「在同一笔交易上多次收钱」,AJ 称这是可怕的利益冲突。

evidence.quote: But also in that moment, the entire industry realizes if I become what's called vertically integrated, I'm not just the administrator, I own the pharmacy.

entities.name: 反向定位 (counterpositioning)
entities.how_described: 本集主持人用它概括 Judy 的打法:所有人都在某个商业模式上赚钱,你用一种更对齐的模式做同样甚至更好的产品。

evidence.quote: This is kind of like classic, you know, counterpositioning, if you want to look at it that way.

entities.name: 自筹资金 (bootstrap)
entities.how_described: 本集说因为没人投这种「无法攻破的堡垒」赛道,他们自筹资金起步:从小规模构建开始、授权第三方软件,熬过最初一两年再建自己设想的平台。

evidence.quote: Yeah, you bootstrap.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And when you bootstrap, you might have this vision of this powerful platform that's going to process claims and administrate patients and workflows.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

entities.name: 进入市场 (go to market)
entities.how_described: 本集把它说成头两年的零营销打法:不赞助、不参会、不在搜索上花钱,钱全砸在呼叫中心和上门服务上,赌「客户会变成我们最好的品牌大使」。

evidence.quote: The first one is really around go to market.

evidence.speaker: Pablo Srugo

entities.name: 理赔处理 (adjudication)
entities.how_described: 本集说 Judy 就是 adjudication 的简称,即理赔处理:数百条管理工作流(资格认定、财务规则、临床规则、账务、呼叫中心等)的和谐运转,而竞争对手很多还在人工拼接不同系统。

evidence.quote: Judy short for adjudication, which is a fancy word for claim processing.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And so adjudication, in order to do it, just to visualize it, is hundreds of administrative workflows, like eligibility, who's in and out of a plan, plan design, like financial rule sets, what's her copay or coinsurance or out-of-pocket max.

entities.name: 工会 (unions)
entities.how_described: 本集说工会是最好的早期客户:想把成员当家人对待,且市政机构和工会有固定预算、必须精确计算福利可持续性,「在前几年,工会成为了我们业务的核心」。

evidence.quote: You know, I often say unions are very good early adopters when it comes to cost savings and service, because one, they want to make sure their membership is treated on a level like family.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: The second part is municipalities and public sector and unions, they have fixed budgets.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: You know, corporate America doesn't necessarily have the same sensitivity to price that unions do for the reason I just described.

evidence.quote: And so unions became at the heart of our business the first couple of years.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: You know, those first two years, you know, I would say I bleed taft-heartly in the sense that I will forever be very thankful for unions.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: Oftentimes, you know, unions in public sector have very good benefits.

entities.name: 价差定价 (spread pricing)
entities.how_described: 本集把它说成传统 PBM 的赚钱方式之一:竞争对手宣称服务免费,实际从药品价差里赚钱;ERISA 修正案要求披露后,按客户拆分价差定价等所有收入流「几乎是不可能的」。

evidence.quote: But my competitors had to suddenly contemplate am I going to disclose what I'm making on spread pricing, acquisition costs, 340B, rebates, performance management fees, you know, they like price protection, they have all these revenue streams.

entities.name: 透明度 (transparency)
entities.how_described: 本集说 2021 年《综合拨款法案》对 ERISA 的修正案要求对医疗保健所有报酬完全披露,2024 年成了「透明度重要的那一年」,所有潜在客户都在问谁是透明的、谁讲道德——这成了 Judy 的一股顺风。

evidence.quote: And so 2024, I often say, was this year in which transparency mattered.
